title: 🔥 Meta launches "Muse Ember" — its smallest and cheapest model for AI agents!
body: 🔥 Meta launches "Muse Ember" — its smallest and cheapest model for AI agents!

Meta launched on November 9 the "Muse Ember" model, its smallest and most efficient model, designed specifically for the work AI agents repeat all day: tool calls, small coding tasks, routing, data extraction, and analysing long documents.

The model costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, runs with a one-million-token context window, and can produce up to 512,000 tokens in a single response. It understands text, images, audio and video together — reading screenshots, charts and scanned documents, or working from audio recordings — without a separate model for each type.

In the "Automation Bench-AA" test for complete business tasks, Ember scored 37.8%, compared with 13.9% for the "Claude Haiku 5.5" model and 20.2% for the "GPT-6 Luna" model, and it matches Haiku's best result at about a third of the cost per task. It is available now via the "Meta Model" interface and in the "Muse Code" tool under the name "Muse-Ember-1.0".

Meta says the model was designed to work alongside its larger model "Muse Wonder": "Wonder plans, and Ember executes the volume." It is the fourth model in the "Muse" family after "Spark", "Glimmer" and "Wonder", and the first model trained using "Muse Wonder Full".

Simply put: imagine a senior engineer drawing the plan, and an army of fast, cheap workers carrying out thousands of small repetitive tasks. Ember is that army — small, fast and cheap, designed for volume, not genius.
Do you prefer a small, cheap model that handles thousands of tasks, or a giant model for one difficult task?
